measurements.label: Tip-to-tip diameter
measurements.method: Steel rule, unfolded on a flat plate

parts.name: Blade pair
parts.role: Two matched carbon blades that produce the thrust.
parts.whatItDoes: Each blade is a twisted wing. As it spins it pushes air down, and the reaction pushes the aircraft up. On a folding propeller each blade pivots at the root so it can swing back when the motor stops.
parts.whyItMatters: The two blades must match in mass and shape. A mismatch of even a few tenths of a gram causes vibration that the flight controller has to fight.
buyingChecks: Buy and replace blades as a matched pair
Ask for the mass tolerance between blades in a pair
Check the leading edge for voids or rough patches
Check rotation direction markings for each motor position

parts.name: Upper hub plate
parts.role: Clamps the blade roots from above.
parts.whatItDoes: One half of the hub clamp. It sandwiches both blade roots against the lower plate and carries the pivot bolts.
parts.whyItMatters: Hub flatness sets whether both blades sit at the same angle. An uneven hub makes one blade do more work than the other.
buyingChecks: Check the hub matches your motor's mounting pattern
Look for burrs where the blade roots sit
Ask for the tightening torque for the pivot bolts

parts.name: Pivot bolts
parts.role: Hold each blade and let it fold.
parts.whatItDoes: Two shoulder bolts pass through the hub plates and the blade roots. Each blade pivots on its bolt.
parts.whyItMatters: Bolt wear lets the blade rock, which causes vibration and can shift balance during flight.
parts.material: Steel shoulder bolts with locking nuts
buyingChecks: Ask whether spare bolts and nuts are sold
Check for locking nuts or thread-locker
Inspect for wear marks at each service

parts.name: Lower hub plate
parts.role: Clamps the blade roots from below and seats on the motor.
parts.whatItDoes: The lower half of the hub clamp. It sits on the motor's bell and locates the propeller on the shaft or bolt pattern.
parts.whyItMatters: If the lower plate is off-centre, the whole propeller spins off-axis, which no amount of blade balancing can fix.
buyingChecks: Check the centre bore matches your motor shaft or adapter
Check the bolt pattern matches your motor
Confirm the plate sits flat on the bell

parts.name: Bore adapter
parts.role: Centres the propeller on the motor shaft.
parts.whatItDoes: A small ring that fits the hub's centre hole to a specific shaft diameter, so one hub can fit several motors.
parts.whyItMatters: A loose adapter lets the propeller sit off-centre, which causes vibration at every speed.
buyingChecks: Check the adapter sizes included match your shaft
Check for a snug fit with no play
Ask whether adapters are sold separately
